blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. clarified that proposed trade deals with Washington are aimed at diversifying the Philippines’ supply sources — not replacing existing partners — following US President Donald Trump’s claim that Manila agreed to source all its agricultural and energy imports from America. During their bilateral meeting in Manila on November 18, Trump said he urged Marcos to purchase US agricultural goods and energy, framing the proposal as a move to erase Washington’s trade deficit with the Philippines.
